description: Specific STAR answers with numbers, clear personal ownership and honest reflection.

messages.text: Hi Asha, I'm Liam. Tell me about yourself.

I graduated in CS this year. At Zeta I owned the nightly reconciliation job for card payments: I rewrote it in Go to stream both files instead of loading them, which cut runtime from six hours to twenty minutes and let ops close books before 9 am.
Tell me about a conflict in a team.

My mentor wanted to patch duplicate refunds with a retry check in the client. I thought the fix belonged on the server, so I asked for a day, wrote a one-page comparison and reproduced the race in a test. We agreed on idempotency keys with a unique index; duplicates went from about 40 a month to zero. I also learned to bring data before opinions.

I shipped a migration that added a column with a default and locked the refunds table for two minutes in production. I flagged it in the incident channel myself, helped roll back, wrote the postmortem, and added a checklist item and a CI lint for locking migrations. Nobody on the team has hit it since.
Tell me about a time you took ownership beyond your role.

Our on-call runbooks were outdated, so in my last month I interviewed three on-call engineers, rewrote six runbooks and ran a game day. Mean time to acknowledge dropped from 15 to 6 minutes the next quarter.
What would you do differently next time?
I'd involve the ops team earlier. On the reconciliation rewrite I only asked them for feedback at the end, and we had to redo the mismatch report format, which cost a week.
Thanks, that's all from me. The team will be in touch.
